title: Assembling a chain-complex splitting from compatible split functionals
statement: Let R be a commutative ring and C an integer-indexed chain complex of R-modules. Fix i, linear functionals α:C_i→R and β:C_(i−1)→R and vectors z∈C_i, w∈C_(i−1). Suppose α(z)=β(w)=1, β(d_i(x))=α(x) for every x, d_i(z)=w, α(d_(i+1)(x))=0 for every x, and d_(i−1)(w)=0. Set S_i=ker α, S_(i−1)=ker β and S_j=C_j (as the top submodule) elsewhere. There are complexes C′ and T, linear equivalences C′_j≃S_j in every degree, and a degreewise binary-direct-sum chain isomorphism C′⊕T≃C [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules]. T is zero outside i,i−1 and its middle differential is the identity on R under specified linear equivalences T_i≃R and T_(i−1)≃R. No finiteness or freeness is assumed.

proof.text: Use split_submodules_stable to prove that the explicit kernel and line families are invariant under every differential. Apply restrictToSubmodules to construct both complexes by restricting the original differentials. Their square-zero relations follow by evaluating C.d_comp_d in the ambient module.

The line terms are the spans R·z and R·w in the two specified degrees and bottom elsewhere. The restrictions of α and β give linear equivalences from these spans to R: the inverse sends r to r·z or r·w. Their composites are identities because α(z)=β(w)=1. The relation βd=α makes the middle differential the identity under these equivalences.

Prove IsCompl(ker α, R·z) and IsCompl(ker β, R·w) using x=(x−α(x)z)+α(x)z and the corresponding formula for β. Elsewhere top and bottom are complementary. Compose DirectSum.linearEquivFunOnFintype, the Boolean-function/product equivalence, and Submodule.prodEquivOfIsCompl to obtain ψ. Its value on the two summands is the sum of their ambient inclusions.

Both complexes have the original differential restricted to their submodules. Thus ψ commutes with the differentials by linearity: d(x+t)=d(x)+d(t). The kernel-term equivalences g are identities. No arbitrary degreewise equivalence or arbitrary existential witness is used.

theorem exists_splitting_of_split_functionals
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (C : ChainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v} R) ℤ)
    (i : ℤ) (α : C.X i →ₗ[R] R) (β : C.X (i - 1) →ₗ[R] R)
    (z : C.X i) (w : C.X (i - 1))
    (hz : α z = 1) (hw : β w = 1)
    (hd : ∀ x, β ((C.d i (i - 1)).hom x) = α x)
    (hdz : (C.d i (i - 1)).hom z = w)
    (hin : ∀ x, α ((C.d (i + 1) i).hom x) = 0)
    (hout : (C.d (i - 1) (i - 2)).hom w = 0) :
    let S : ∀ j : ℤ, Submodule R (C.X j) := fun j ↦
      if h : j = i then h ▸ LinearMap.ker α
      else if h : j = i - 1 then h ▸ LinearMap.ker β else ⊤
    ∃ (C' T : ChainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v} R) ℤ)
      (g : ∀ j, C'.X j ≃ₗ[R] S j),
      (∀ j : ℤ, j ≠ i → j ≠ i - 1 → Subsingleton (T.X j)) ∧
      ∃ (e : T.X i ≃ₗ[R] R) (f : T.X (i - 1) ≃ₗ[R] R),
        (∀ t : T.X i, f ((T.d i (i - 1)).hom t) = e t) ∧
        let M : ℤ → Bool → ModuleCat.{max u v} R :=
          fun j s ↦ if s then T.X j else C'.X j
        ∃ ψ : ∀ j : ℤ, (⨁ s : Bool, M j s) ≃ₗ[R] C.X j,
          ∀ (j : ℤ) (x : C'.X j) (t : T.X j),
            (C.d j (j - 1)).hom
                (ψ j (DirectSum.lof R Bool (fun s ↦ M j s) false x +
                  DirectSum.lof R Bool (fun s ↦ M j s) true t)) =
              ψ (j - 1)
                (DirectSum.lof R Bool (fun s ↦ M (j - 1) s) false
                    ((C'.d j (j - 1)).hom x) +
                  DirectSum.lof R Bool (fun s ↦ M (j - 1) s) true
                    ((T.d j (j - 1)).hom t))
